messages.author: 319087d95952828f
messages.subject: log_prob-methods
parts:
Hi Everyone,

I'm currently trying to implement an HMC experiment outside of stan but would like to use stan to evaluate the log-probability and its gradient.  I found the log_prob-methods section in the rstan manual and would like some clarification on the following excerpt from the 'Details' section before I proceed:

However, when using the log density function for a model exposed to R, we need to be careful. For example, if we are interested in finding the mode of parameters on the constrained space, we then do not need the adjustment. For this reason, there is an argument named adjust_transform for functions log_prob and grad_log_prob.

 At the end of the day, I would like the log-probability evaluated on the constrained parameters.  After some tooling around, I settled on first getting the unconstrained transformed parameters and then plugging them into log_prob with 'adjust_transform = FALSE'.  Here is an example with a simple exponential distribution model:

test_model <- stan_model('log_prob_test.stan')
test             <- sampling(test_model, data=list(y=1), iter=1, chains=1)
un               <- unconstrain_pars(test, pars=list(lambda=2))
log_prob(test, upars=un,adjust_transform=FALSE)

It gave me what I wanted for the simple model, but are there any issues I should know about in general?  I will be using these log-probabilities as part of the accept/reject step, so I intuit that the log-Jacobians should not be included.


Next, I want to evaluate the gradient.  After playing around I'm under the impression that 

grad_log_prob(test,upars=un,adjust_transform=TRUE)

will give me the gradient of the log-probability plus log Jacobian.  It seems correct to take the unconstrained transformation into account in this way.  But am I wrong to use the transform when evaluating the gradient but not for the log-probability?  Keep in mind I will be using these values within HMC.

Thanks in advance,
Andrew

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] log_prob-methods
parts:
If you want to do HMC (or random-walk Metropolis) in the unconstrained space,
then you need the Jacobians in the gradients and in the Metropolis
accept/reject step.

But, the log densities drop constant terms (additive terms in the log density
only involving constants and data as declared in the data block).

If you really need the log density on the constrained parameters without
the Jacobian, then you have to evaluate that with propto=false in the C++
template to avoid dropping constant terms. I'm not sure how to do this
through RStan; internally, Stan doesn't care about the constant terms.

- Bob

Yes. If you take a positive-constrained parameter, you
should be able to see the effect (the log Jacobian is just
the parameter value, so that should be how much the difference
is with a single positive-constrained parameter).
